title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: Adam's first actual not by nature owed to all as corrupting imputation
pass_a_gloss: Adam's first actual deed, though the serpent authored it, did not by nature earn everyone's moral ruin, nor was it by nature such that justice could not leave it uncharged to all when fixing that vice in them. Call it such by nature and you quit the great defenders who share your imputation—and Placeus will thank you if you teach and prove it.
pass_b_english: But that first actual sin of Adam, whose author the serpent himself was, did not by its nature merit the moral corruption of all humans, nor was it by its nature of such a kind that, divine justice being preserved, it could not but be imputed to all humans unto fixing that vice in them. And if you think it was such by nature, you will also depart from the opinion of the great men who with you defend that imputation, and you will do us a great favor if you teach and prove it.
source_text: At peccatum illud primum actuale Adami, cujus ipsi author serpens fuit, natura sua non merebatur omnium hominum corruptionem moralem, nec erat natura sua ejusmodi, ut salva divina justitia non posset non imputari omnibus hominibus ad illud vitium ipsis infigendum. Quod si putes tale fuisse natura, & discedes a sententia magnorum virorum qui tecum imputationem illam tuentur, & pergratum nobis feceris, si id docueris & probaveris.
